messages.author: bc55224057ef2ffa
messages.subject: Trouble with NA's in gdistsamp
parts:
Hello unmarked community-

I am using gdistsamp to analyze 3 years worth of distance sampling data  using the stacked data structure, as suggested by Andy (https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/unmarked/which$20method/unmarked/DvliCEn91BI/XsapvLGOEQAJ). Briefly, I had 21 sites, ideally with 3 visits within a year. Data is stacked so 'sites' are 'site-year' and replicates are the three visits within a year. Not every site was visited three times per year due to weather etc, which results in having NA's in both the detection history (y) and the detection variables (yearlySiteCovs). 

I am able to fit models, with what seem to be reasonable values for the coefficients, get values from ranef, and get predicted values from'predict with a null model or with an abundance only model. However, once there are detection variables in the model, I can no longer use ranef or do a GOF test. I get the error:

Error in integrate(grhaz, db[j], db[j + 1], shape = shape[i, t], scale = scale,  : 
  non-finite function value
  
With help from John Clare, he found that if the missing values in yearlySiteCovs were replaced, then these methods worked for models with detection variables. The error appears to come from trying to integrate over the NA values in yearlySiteCovs.

Has anyone else had an issue like this? If there are NA's in the appropriate slots in 'y' in the unmarkedFrameGDS, then are the imputed values within yearlySiteCovs not used for calculating density estimates, coefficients, etc? Maybe there are larger issues at play here? 

I'd be happy to provide the dataset if anyone is interested. Thanks in advance for any guidance!

Max
